decision: The guards that rely on read-then-write, each with its mechanism: (1) a reminder's claim — the unique index reminderSent_claim_idx (kind, target kind, target, anchor day, offset) and INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING in the transaction that writes the message, notifications and deliveries; (2) the target still owed / unverified — the target rows locked FOR SHARE in id order, then read again in a statement of its own (READ COMMITTED: it sees what committed while the lock waited); (3) a scheduled message's send — its row FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED with its status read again under the lock, plus the unique delivery per (message, recipient, channel, student); (4) a cancel — the message row FOR UPDATE before its status is read; (5) an email's send — the status-guarded claim queued -> sending; (6) an interrupted email — a status-guarded update to failed, never requeued; (7) a rule's change — the rule row FOR UPDATE before it is read (the audit's 'before'), a racing create refused by the unique index; (8) a template's change — its row FOR UPDATE. Every send, schedule, cancel, rule and template change writes its audit row inside its transaction (logAction(..., tx))
